newsitem.title: USA: Marco regroups, storm warnings up for Cuba.
newsitem.headline: Marco regroups, storm warnings up for Cuba.

text.p: Former hurricane Marco revved up once again in the Caribbean on Monday, reaching tropical storm strength and heading for Cuba, still recovering from hurricane Lili's pounding in mid October, the National Hurricane Centre said.

At 4 p.m. EST (2100 GMT), the centre of Marco was located at latitude 19.5 north, longitude 83.9 west, about 175 miles (285 km) south-southeast of Cabo San Antonio on the western tip of Cuba, and moving northwest at 13 mph (20 kph).

A tropical storm warning was in effect for the Isle of Youth and the Pinar del Rio province of western Cuba. Forecasters said heavy rains were spreading over the Isle of Youth and would hit the mainland in the next day or so.
The storm had maximum sustained winds near 50 mph (80 kph) and was expected to weaken in the next 24 hours, forecasters said.

Marco, a late-season storm spawned in the Caribbean Sea off the Central America coast last week, has waxed and waned wildly. It grew to hurricane strength at midweek with maximum winds of 75 mph (120 kph), only to fade to a tropical depression during the weekend.
The storm left two dead in Nicaragua last week when flooding from heavy rains washed away homes on the Pacific coast and northern regions.
Hurricane Lili pounded the central and western regions of Cuba on Oct. 17-18 destroying some 5,000 homes and damaging crops, power lines and communications.
The Atlantic hurricane season officially ends on Saturday.
